data.source_title: Applying Lean methodologies reduces ED laboratory turnaround times
data.locator: Abstract, Methods and Results; full-text sections listed as Introduction, Methods, Results and Limitations
data.source_setting: Massachusetts General Hospital teaching-hospital emergency department and laboratory, Boston, Massachusetts
data.source_period: Prospective before-after intervention; exact observation dates and per-test counts not available in accessible article abstract
data.source_n: Six ED tests; exact test counts not stated in accessible abstract
data.quantity: Observed median collection-to-result TAT before and after workflow redesign
data.unit: minutes (medians; reduction values reported with 99% confidence intervals)
data.source_evidence_basis: Prospective before-after study reports median collection-to-result turnaround. Lean sample-flow reorganization without added resources reduced troponin T from 86 to 53 minutes (33-minute decrease; 99% CI 30-35) and urine sedimentation from 117 to 29 minutes (88-minute decrease; 99% CI 87-90).
data.limitations: Single teaching ED, intervention study, six selected tests; not randomized. Accessible abstract does not expose sample counts or exact dates. Results describe medians and must not be treated as a service-time distribution.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Separate collection, transport, accession, analysis, reflex-test, and result-report stages; reflex testing can add a second queue. Use medians only as external plausibility checks, not as a fitted distribution or RWJ target.
data.retrieval_timestamp_precision: day; time not logged during source inspection, midnight is a date placeholder
